introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The following equation represents a reversible reaction used in an industrial process.

$\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_3(g)}$   $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$
incertitudes: Points imprimés 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10, conformes au total. Le sujet écrit « KJ/mol » : transcrit « kJ/mol ».

En-tête de la Section A : « ANSWER ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 answers » ; modélisé en « 4 sur 5 » (toutes tentées, 4 meilleures notées). Section B : « ANSWER ALL 2 questions » modélisé en « 2 sur 2 ». Section C : « 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3 » (si plus de 2 tentées, seules les deux premières comptent).

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the source of nitrogen and hydrogen. Nitrogen: ......... Hydrogen: ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Nitrogen:** the **air** (obtained by fractional distillation of liquid air; air is about 78% nitrogen).

**Hydrogen:** **natural gas (methane)** reacting with steam, or from cracking of petroleum fractions (also possible: electrolysis of water).

questions.enonce_markdown: What is a reversible reaction? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: A reversible reaction is one in which the **products can react to re-form the reactants**, so the reaction can go in both the forward and the backward direction (shown by $\rightleftharpoons$).

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the enthalpy change for the backward reaction? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The backward reaction has the same size but the opposite sign: $\Delta H = \mathbf{+92\ kJ/mol}$ (endothermic).

questions.enonce_markdown:
State what will happen to the yield of ammonia, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, when:

(i) The temperature is increased

(ii) The pressure is decreased *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The forward reaction is **exothermic** ($\Delta H = -92$ kJ/mol), so raising the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the left: the yield of ammonia **decreases**.

(ii) There are 4 moles of gas on the left ($1 + 3$) and 2 moles on the right. Decreasing the pressure favours the side with more gas molecules (the left): the yield of ammonia **decreases**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The reaction is usually catalysed:

(i) Identify the catalyst

(ii) State the role played by the catalyst. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Iron** (finely divided iron, in the Haber process).

(ii) It **speeds up the reaction** (lowers the activation energy) so that equilibrium is reached faster; it does **not** change the position of equilibrium or the yield.

**Le Chatelier's principle:** if a change is made to the conditions (concentration, pressure or temperature) of a system **in dynamic equilibrium**, the position of equilibrium shifts in the direction that **opposes (counteracts) the change**.
